title: Run Kaggle and Hugging Face against the live services
request: With the owner's approval for each download, import one small public dataset from Hugging Face and one from Kaggle through the 'Bring the data' card; say the dataset, its licence and size before downloading; check the recorded source, licence, revision and SHA-256 and that no credential appears in the draft; fix what the live services do differently from the fakes.
spec: Done when one small public dataset from each service is imported through the page with its licence and SHA-256 recorded.
plan: Look up a small public Hugging Face dataset and its licence and size without downloading.
Ask the owner to approve the one download (scikit-learn/iris, CC0-1.0, one CSV of a few KB, no token).
Import it through the draft route the card calls on a temporary server.
Check the asset's source URL, licence, revision, file hash, the pipeline result, and that no credential is in the draft.
Leave Kaggle open until a key and an approved dataset exist.

decisions.decision: Each download waits for the owner's explicit yes.
decisions.why: A download fetches outside content onto the machine.

decisions.decision: The import went through the API route the card calls, not by clicking the card.
decisions.why: It exercises the same server path; the row says so.

change: No code change: a live import through POST /api/drafts/{id}/data/hf.

measurements.name: Hugging Face live import
measurements.gate: One small public dataset imported with licence, revision and SHA-256 recorded and no credential in the draft.
measurements.result: scikit-learn/iris: licence cc0-1.0, revision main pinned to its commit, one file Iris.csv of 5,107 bytes with its SHA-256 and source URL recorded; 150 rows by 6 columns, cleaned and analysed in about 3 seconds; no credential in the draft. The live service behaved as the fakes did.
measurements.against_gate: The gate asks for one small public dataset with licence, revision and SHA-256 recorded and no credential in the draft. scikit-learn/iris came in with licence cc0-1.0, revision main pinned to its commit, Iris.csv of 5,107 bytes with its SHA-256 and source URL, 150 rows by 6 columns, and no credential: it passes.
limits: One tiny public dataset with no token; gated data, configs, splits and large files were not tried live.
The import went through the API route the card calls, not by clicking the card in a browser.
It shows the live service matched the fakes for this dataset only.

measurements.name: Kaggle live import
measurements.gate: One small public dataset imported with licence and SHA-256 recorded.
measurements.result: Not run: KAGGLE_USERNAME and KAGGLE_KEY are not configured and no dataset has been approved.
measurements.next: Run once the owner adds a Kaggle key and approves a dataset.
measurements.against_gate: Nothing ran: no Kaggle key is configured and no dataset was approved, so there is no number to set against the gate.
limits: The Kaggle connector has only met fakes; its assumptions about the API's field names and about a whole dataset arriving as a zip are unchecked.
Until a key exists, the Kaggle tab on Home has not been exercised end to end.

outcome: Hugging Face done; Kaggle open. Nothing needed fixing: the live Hugging Face service matched the fakes in tests/test_connectors.py.
lessons: Before a live check, state the dataset, licence and size and get a yes; then check the recorded provenance, not only that rows arrived.
risks: A download brings outside content onto the machine; it needs the owner's yes, with the dataset, licence and size stated first.
The live service may differ from the fakes in field names, file layout or how a revision is pinned.
Checking only that rows arrived would miss a wrong licence, revision or hash in the record.
A token or key could end up in the draft's recorded source.
